query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

per_column.name: primary_issue_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes the free-text short_description into clean issue types, giving a strong new grouping axis. Sampled values (database_access, vpn_connectivity, network_connectivity, software_system) are all sound readings of the source text. Somewhat overlaps with the existing 'category' column but adds finer text-derived granularity.

per_column.name: issue_severity_signal
per_column.rationale: A severity/nature dimension is genuinely useful for prioritization analysis. However some labels are not well-grounded: 'Unable to access the database' -> access_failure_individual is fine, but 'VPN issue, frequent disconnection' -> service_degradation_partial and 'Software update issue' -> access_failure_individual read as guesses beyond the terse text; individual-vs-outage scope is asserted where the text is silent.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Almost certainly redundant with the existing 'assigned_to'/'closed_by' original columns, so it adds little new analytical leverage. The specific technician names are not derivable from the sampled source_text (which only exposes timestamps and short_description); the value appears copied from an unshown column or invented, and cannot be validated from the provided evidence.

per_column.name: location_or_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope is a plausibly useful axis, and the large <NULL> share (238) correctly reflects silence. But non-null assignments are weakly grounded: 'Unable to access the database' -> device_individual and 'Unable to access the company's intranet' -> office_wide impose a scope the terse text does not state, so many concrete values are unwarranted inferences.

per_column.name: issue_recurrence_pattern
per_column.rationale: Recurrence would be useful if grounded, but the values contradict the text. 'Unable to access the database' and 'Unable to access the company's intranet' -> systemic_recurring have no recurrence signal in the source; only 'frequent disconnection' warrants a recurring label. The distinctions (systemic vs same_user vs same_system) are largely fabricated for single-line tickets.

per_column.name: same_person_assigned_closed
per_column.rationale: A boolean comparing assigned_to and closed_by is a legitimate process/workflow metric derivable from original columns. It is not verifiable from the sampled source_text (those columns aren't shown), but it is a clearly warranted mechanical derivation from existing fields, so no fabrication is assumed.

judge.rationale: The added set offers several genuinely useful analytical axes (issue category, severity, workflow same-person flag), improving on the raw ticket text. The main weakness is groundedness: severity, location/scope, and especially recurrence assign confident specific labels to extremely terse single-line descriptions that do not support them, and assigned_technician is both redundant with existing columns and unverifiable from the shown text. primary_issue_category is the strongest column; issue_recurrence_pattern is the weakest due to systematic over-assertion of recurrence.
